Laura — drafting some technical language to drop straight into the spreadsheet. Notes below are targeted at the questionnaire sections where we usually see gaps.

1) Transfer mechanisms & routing policies
- Default: requests from EU are routed to the nearest compatible model variant; backend compute may be in US, EU, or APAC depending on customer tenancy and capacity.
- Controls: SCCs implemented for controller-processor relationships; fallbacks to Dedicated/Private for customers requiring physical residency.

Suggested wording: "Redwood employs contractual safeguards (SCCs) and technical routing controls to ensure that EU personal data is processed under adequate transfer mechanisms. Customers may select Dedicated or Private deployments for data residency requirements."

2) KMS & key custody
- We use cloud HSM-backed KMS for platform keys; customer-managed CMKs available for Private/Dedicated.
- Keys used for at-rest encryption and optional token-level wrapping of secrets; access restricted via IAM roles and audited.

Suggested wording: "Platform keys are protected in HSM-backed KMS; for Private or Dedicated deployments, customers can supply/manage their own customer master keys (CMKs) to minimize Redwood-held key access."

3) Logging / retention / audit evidence
- We can provide sample redacted traces showing request provenance and model variant selection, and summarized latency/cost breakdowns. Retention defaults: application logs 90 days, platform audit logs 365 days (extendable via paid add-on).

4) Network & segmentation
- Provide VPC diagrams with subnet separation for tenant compute, control plane, and management. We should attach an updated network-segmentation.pdf that reflects recent changes to our control plane isolation.

5) DPA annex specifics to include
- Subprocessor list, routing policy clause, technical/organizational measures table, KMS/custody options, data deletion obligations on termination.

I will attach a short snippet for the KMS paragraph and a tracing artifact to the draft spreadsheet. Ben, can you confirm the retention numbers and whether Legal wants us to phrase SCCs vs DPF as "supplementary measures"?
